newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas continues firmer as volumes tail off.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas continues firmer as volumes tail off.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract barely traded on Thursday afternoon, although prices continued to tick up in the small number of deals done.

June was traded at 10.40 pence a therm, up by 0.075 pence from Wednesday's settlement, while December traded again at 14.45 pence, up a further 0.05 pence from the morning and giving a total rise of 0.21 pence from the previous settlement price.
Only 20 lots were done in the afternoon session, a total of 95 for the day - down from 525 lots earlier in the week.

"It's all slowing down again. In volume terms it's doing next to nothing now," said a futures broker. He added that some major gas companies were "a bit despondent" about the apparent difficulty of getting trades concluded at all in such a thin market.

Trade was only seen in four months, June, December, January and February, and the futures market is tracking the physical market in that trade is moving away from the front month with more interest being seen for next winter.
This pattern was seen on the OTC market when a problem on an Amoco compression platform, which had sent prompt prices firmer, was resolved and saw interest switch to the winter.
